caption:
Anthropic says AI agents directed by its employees now log six times as many hours as the employees themselves.
The share of junior hires in its technical teams fell from 27% to 9%.
Some staff say their job is shifting from doing the work to managing Claudes.

Would you rather do the work or manage the AI that does it?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic

slides.headline: Inside Anthropic, AI agents now outwork humans *6 to 1*. Junior hiring just plunged

slides.heading: Agents *outwork* people
paras: By August 2026, AI agents directed by Anthropic employees logged six times as many hours as the employees themselves, the company said in a new report.
Combined agent work hours first passed human work hours in March 2026.

slides.heading: Fewer *junior* hires
paras: The share of junior hires in Anthropic's technical departments fell from 27% to 9%. Junior staff in those teams dropped from 21% to 14% since early 2025.
Postings for junior roles fell sharply after December 2025.

slides.heading: From doing to *managing*
paras: Code commits per engineer are five times what they were six months earlier. One engineer described "an army of Claudes, with every one asking for my attention."
In an April survey, 20% of written answers described shifting from doing the work to managing Claudes.

slides.heading: A very different *2030*
paras: Anthropic employees expect AI to do 75% of their work by 2030, compared with 28% for other Americans.

paras.t: Anthropic cautions that an AI lab is not a typical business, so its experience may not carry over to other companies.

slides.hook: AI is reshaping jobs at Anthropic first. Follow to see what reaches your job next.
